senses.gloss: (b. h.; cmp. חלל)to be lax, to be sick, faint away, grieve.
units: <cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 43:3">Ex. R. s. 43</cite> (expl. <he>ויחל</he>, <cite ref="Exodus 32:11">Ex. XXXII, 11</cite> <he>ח׳ משה</he> Moses was sick (grieved).
<cite ref="Kiddushin 71b">Kidd. 71ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>מדי חוֹלָה</he> Media is sick, v. <cite ref="C00451"><he>גּוֹסֵס</he></cite>.—
<cite ref="Berakhot 28b:6">Ber. 28ᵇ</cite> <he>כשח׳ וכ׳</he> when R. … fell sick; a. fr.—V. <cite ref="H00333"><he>חוֹלֶה</he></cite>.

senses.gloss: to soften, sweeten; to soothe, assuage (by prayer, gifts &c.). Ex. R. l. c. מהו וַיְחַל שהכניס וכ׳ what does vayḥal (Ex. l. c.) mean? He offered &c. (ref. to Ps. XLV, 13).
units: <cite ref="Psalms 45:13">Ib.</cite> <he>מהו ויחל עשה את המר וכ׳</he> he made sweet what was bitter.
<cite ref="Psalms 45:13">Ib.</cite> <he>חַלֵּי מרירתן וכ׳</he> sweeten thou the bitterness (sin) of Israel &c.—
<cite ref="Psalms 45:13">Ib.</cite> <he>מי שיְחַלֶּה וכ׳</he> one to sweeten the bitterness &c. (by prayer).
Yalk. Ex. 392 אביי אמר עד שחִילֵּהוּ להקב״ה בתפילתו (v. infra) Ab. explained vayḥal, until he assuaged (the anger of) the Lord &c.
<cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 3:15">Deut. R. s. 3</cite> <he>הרי בניך מרים חַלֵּה אותן</he> thy children are bitter, sweeten them.

<cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 3:15">Ib.</cite> <he>היאך יהא א״ל הוי חל אתה רחמים</he>, read: <he>היאך אהא אומר א״ל הוי אומר חַלֵּה את המרים</he> what shall I say? Said He, Say, sweeten &c.; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 392:2">Yalk. Ex. 392</cite>.

<cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 1:26">Lam. R. to I, 2</cite> <he>לא חִלִּינוּ פניך</he> we did not assuage thee by repentance; <cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 45">Ex. R. s. 45</cite> <he>חלִּינוּ מלפני הקב״ה</he> we prayed &c.; a. fr.

<cite ref="Berakhot 32a">Ber. 32ᵃ</cite> <he>אביי אמר עד שהֶחֱלֵהוּ להקב״ה בתפלה</he> Ms. M. (v. D. S. a. l.) until he assuaged &c., v. supra. [<cite ref="Berakhot 32a">Ib.</cite> <he>שה׳ עליהם וכ׳</he>, read: <he>שהֵחֵל</he>, v. <cite ref="H01073"><he>חָלַל</he></cite>.]

senses.gloss: to make sick, wear out. Ib. עמד משה … עד שהחלהו (Ms. M. עד שחלה) Moses stood in prayer … until He wore Him out (by his persistency, v. Rashi a. l. a. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 3).—3) (v. חָלַל a. חִלְחֵל) to permeate, affect.
units: B. Mets. 107ᵇ bile is called maḥlah (v. מַחְלָה) שהיא מַחְלָה וכ׳ (Ms. F. שמְחַלֶּלֶת) for it goes through the entire body [perh. מְחַלָּה, fr. חָלַל].

senses.gloss: to be made sick. Ber. l. c. עמד … עד שה׳ ed. Sonc. a. oth. (v. supra) until He was worn out.
